chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from al-'Ammi via his chain who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The Almighty Allah will not accept the repentance of the possessor of innovation.' It was asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, how is that?' He replied, 'Because his heart has been imbued with its love.'
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah not accept the repentance of someone who introduces religious innovation?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, this narration highlights the spiritualizes the rejection of repentance by attributing it to the heart's deep saturation with the love of the innovation itself, rather than a divine decree of impossibility. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *bid'ah* as a corruption of inner conviction that obscures the soul's capacity to turn back to Allah, distinguishing it from mere external error.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 5. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan from Muhammad b. al-Hassan al-Saffar from Ya’qub b. Yazid from al-’Ama by his chain who said:

“The Almighty Allah will not accept the repentance of a person who starts an innovation.” He was asked, “Why is it so?” He replied, “It is because the person has kept the love of innovation in his heart.”
